name: Hims & Hers Health, Inc.
business: Hims & Hers runs a subscription telehealth platform selling prescription and wellness treatments (weight loss, sexual health, hair, dermatology, mental health) directly to consumers.

events.what: Acquisition of Eucalyptus (Australia-based digital health; Australia, UK, Germany, Canada, Japan) closed; up to $1.15B aggregate consideration, about 17% of market cap; running at break-even to moderate losses per CFO; no Item 2.01 or 1.01 8-K returned
events.source: 10-Q for quarter ended 2026-06-30, document_id 131752 (Risk Factors: closed June 1, 2026, up to $1.15 billion)

events.what: COO change: Nader Kabbani to advisory role; Mike Chi (Hims since April 2021, previously Chief Commercial Officer) appointed COO
events.from: Hims & Hers Chief Commercial Officer; earlier CMO at Zola

events.source: 10-Q document_id 37744 (month only stated; day not given)

next_event.source: No Investor Day found in Baba for 2026. CFO declined to speak to 2027 yet (Q2 2026 call, 2026-08-10, document_id 131674); the company is moving to an annual shareholder letter (Q1 2026 call, document_id 187001). Q3 2026 results date not sourced.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Target is dollars plus implied level: at least $6.5B revenue and $1.3B adjusted EBITDA by 2030 (20%), set by the CEO on 2025-05-05 and repeated by CFO and CEO every quarter since; it succeeds a 2024 'at least 20% no later than 2030' margin goal (CFO, Q2 2024 call, doc 50887 search hit) and an older 20% to 30% long-term range. Near term runs the other way: FY2026 guide cut from $300M to $375M (Q4 2025 call) to $275M to $325M, about 9% margin (Q2 2026 call), on branded weight loss and international mix. Calendar fiscal year, no label shift.

statements.quote: Consistent execution is allowing us to confidently outline new long-term financial objectives. By 2030, we expect to generate at least $6.5 billion in revenue and $1.3 billion in adjusted EBITDA.
statements.speaker: Andrew Dudum
statements.doc_title: Hims & Hers Health Inc Q1 2025 Earnings Call

statements.quote: This supports our continued confidence in the 2030 ambitions we outlined last year. It'll be $6.5 billion in revenue and $1.3 billion in adjusted EBITDA.
statements.speaker: Yemi Okupe
statements.doc_title: Hims & Hers Health Inc Q1 2026 Earnings Call

statements.quote: It is our expectation that 2026 adjusted EBITDA will be between $275 million and $325 million. These adjusted EBITDA and revenue ranges imply an adjusted EBITDA margin of 9% at the midpoint of both ranges.
statements.speaker: Yemi Okupe
statements.doc_title: Hims & Hers Health Inc Q2 2026 Earnings Call

street.gap_assumption: Like for like: management's implied 20% adjusted EBITDA margin in 2030 ($1.3B / $6.5B) vs VA consensus FY2030 EBITDA / revenue ($753M / $5.01B). FY2030 consensus revenue sits below FY2029 ($5.10B), which points to thin long-dated coverage; the dollar gap ($753M vs $1.3B) is larger than the margin gap.
street.source: Baba data_financials summary consensus (Visible Alpha), fetched 2026-10-01

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q1 2026, Q2 2026]. Q1 from Baba VA actuals (7.3% vs 15.5%); Q2 uses the CFO's rounded 8% (doc 131674) vs the VA Q2 2025 actual of 15.1%. Q3 2026 guide is 10% at the midpoint. Margins are falling by choice (branded GLP-1 and international mix, reinvestment), and the 12-month forward EBITDA revision is -18% even as revenue estimates rose 25%.

verdict: The rubric says 8, but this is a weak GXO match: a founder CEO with no reset, a 2030 20% EBITDA target set in 2025, and margins halved by choice. The 500 bps street gap reflects credibility, not neglect.
open_questions: Is the 2030 target still intact after the FY2026 EBITDA guide was cut twice, and will management restate it with 2027 guidance?
How much of the street gap is thin FY2030 coverage (consensus revenue falls from FY2029 to FY2030) rather than real disbelief?
Does regulatory risk on compounded GLP-1 and peptide offerings cap the margin path regardless of scale?
